To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bias and the variance of the optimal Bayesian-mean decoder can be approximated as the sum of a prior-driven and an encoding-driven term, and that these terms have opposite signs if the encoding is efficient.

(1) the Bayesian mean is biased, and that the bias comprises a component due to the prior, and a component due to precision, and that the relative strengths of the two components are determined by the task at hand, (2) under the same assumptions, the bias is proportional to the derivative of the variance of the decoder, and that the proportionality constant depends on the task.

1) the bias of the optimal decoder is determined by the precision of encoding, 2) the variance of the optimal decoder depends on the task, and 3) the bias-variance relation of the optimal decoder varies across tasks, and can be either Bayesian or anti-Bayesian.

the question of how to optimally encode and decode information.
a general theory of optimal Bayesian decoding, and with its application to the understanding of perception.

the Bayesian mean is a good decoder for a large variety of tasks, and is the best one for the ones that are most commonly encountered.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bias of the optimal Bayesian-mean decoder is a consequence of the task at hand, and is not a consequence of the prior.
the Bayesian-mean decoder is optimal for estimation, but sub-optimal for discrimination.

, under the minimal assumptions of our model, the variance and bias of the Bayesian-mean estimator can be accurately predicted by two parameters: the precision of the stimulus representation in the internal signal, and the derivative of this precision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian mean is biased, in the small-noises regime, and that this bias can be either pro- or anti-Bayesian.
the Bayesian mean is not always biased towards the prior; the direction of the bias depends on the task that the observer is facing.
the Bayesian mean is not a universal estimator, and that it should not be assumed that a Bayesian mean decoder is optimal in all situations.
